concept_summary: The fantasy of Onboarding rebuilt five times because day-one retention was 25 percent stretched over a single persistent season lasting months: one meaningful decision per evening, no grinding, no catching up. Progress compounds across real calendar time and a missed week bends the story instead of ending it. The finale is scheduled, shared, and unrepeatable.
first_experiment: Concierge test: run the core decision by hand over seven daily messages with three players; if day-seven return beats the source's second-session return, the long form has legs.
source_idea_title: Onboarding rebuilt five times because day-one retention was 25 percent
why_it_is_opposite: While the source fits short sessions, this concept flips the clock: one season here outlasts hundreds of source sessions, so the source habit of quick payoff actively hurts.

concept_summary: A reverse-loop game in the world of Visible combo multiplier as the whole retention spine: you begin holding everything the source hands out and win by giving it all back. Where the source loop is 'Arcade space shooter where consecutive hits raise a damage multiplier in visible tiers and any miss resets it to zero, with escalating screen effects per tier.', here every move undoes the 'Arcade space shooter where consecutive hits raise a damage multiplier in visible tiers and any miss resets it to zero, with escalating screen effects per tier.' loop step by step instead of advancing it, so the map empties and the score falls. Hoarding triggers the lose state; the end screen celebrates an empty board.
first_experiment: Paper prototype: ten tokens stand in for everything the player owns and each turn must discard at least one; test with five players whether emptying the board feels like winning after three rounds.
source_idea_title: Visible combo multiplier as the whole retention spine
why_it_is_opposite: While the source rewards accumulation (Arcade space shooter where consecutive hits raise a damage multiplier in visible tiers and any miss resets it to zero, with escalating screen effects per tier.), this concept rewards the opposite: progress means having less, so a winning run here would score zero in the source.

concept_summary: The same core loop as Instant-play pages competing on first frame, not on features, rebuilt end to end for hardcore instead of casual players. Controls, difficulty, session shape, and rewards assume hardcore: permadeath, no assists, and a public skill rating. Nothing in this build serves the old crowd; one client cannot satisfy both.
first_experiment: Take one level from the source fantasy, apply the inverted tuning only, and playtest with five target players for ten minutes; a quit-rate on the opposite side of half from the source baseline confirms the audience split is real.
source_idea_title: Instant-play pages competing on first frame, not on features
why_it_is_opposite: While the source is tuned for casual players (Casual players arriving from a shared link on whatever device is at hand: gentle assists, no fail states, and bite-size sessions), this concept flips every tuning decision toward hardcore (permadeath, no assists, and a public skill rating), so the two builds want mutually exclusive players.
